modules.name: tactility.app
modules.title: App manager
modules.summary: List, launch, stop, install and uninstall apps.

entries.name: list
entries.description: Every registered app, hidden ones included.

entries.name: current
entries.description: The topmost active app id, or nil.

entries.name: start
entries.description:
The new app runs normally (its own task and window); this call returns as soon as
it is scheduled. Arguments are copied by the app module before it returns.

entries.name: stop
entries.description:
Accepts the instance id returned by start() or an app id, in which case the most
recently started running instance is stopped. Refuses to stop the app that runs the script.

entries.name: install
entries.description: Installs a .app package.

entries.name: address
entries.description: The device-tree address: a bus address, an index, or an offset, depending on the device.

modules.name: tactility.display
modules.title: Display
modules.summary: Panel resolution, shape and backlight.

entries.name: brightness
entries.description: Raw backlight level, for diagnostics. Most scripts want the percentage.

entries.name: set_brightness_percent
entries.description: 0 is the dimmest level that stays on.

modules.name: tactility.fs
modules.title: Filesystem
modules.summary: Whole-file reads and writes, directory listing and the file/folder picker.

entries.name: read
entries.description:
Reads a whole file and returns it as a string, or nil plus a reason.

Whole-file only, deliberately: a script holding a FILE* across yields would hold the
mount's mutex with it, which on a shared bus stalls the display. Streaming would need
a handle type with its own lifetime rules - worth adding only if something needs it.

entries.name: list
entries.description:
Lists a directory as an array of { name, directory } tables.

"." and ".." are skipped: every caller has to filter them out, and a script that
recurses without noticing them loops forever.

entries.name: remove
entries.description: Removes a file or an empty directory. Recursive removal is left to the script.

entries.name: mounts
entries.description: The mounted filesystem roots, so a script can find the SD card without guessing.

entries.name: user_data_path
entries.description: Where an app should keep data that survives an OS upgrade.

entries.name: pick_file
entries.description:
Shows the native file dialog. The callback receives the picked path, or
`nil, "cancelled"` when the person cancels. `options.extensions` limits the list,
`options.path` sets the starting directory, `options.name` prefills a save-as name
and `options.allow_new` permits a name that does not exist yet.

entries.name: pick_files
entries.description: Like pick_file(), but the callback receives an array of paths.

entries.name: pick_folder
entries.description:
Shows the folder picker; the callback receives the folder that was shown when
Select was pressed.

modules.name: tactility.log
modules.title: Logging
modules.summary: Write to the device log.

modules.name: tactility.notification
modules.title: Notifications
modules.summary: Post and dismiss notifications, and subscribe to the event stream.

entries.name: send
entries.description: `tactility.notification.send{ message, title?, severity?, sticky?, source?, service? }`

entries.name: list
entries.description: Newest first.

entries.name: dismiss_non_sticky
entries.description: Dismisses the notifications that are not sticky, leaving the sender's own alone.

entries.name: subscribe
entries.description: Receives posted/dismissed/cleared/updated events on the LVGL task. Keep the returned Subscription alive; call cancel() to stop.

modules.name: tactility.power
modules.title: Power
modules.summary: Battery state and charging control.

entries.name: is_available
entries.description: True when a power supply exists at all, so a script can adapt rather than error.

entries.name: capabilities
entries.description:
Everything the board's power supply can do, as a table of booleans.

Lets a UI hide controls it cannot drive instead of showing them and failing.

entries.name: capacity
entries.description: Battery charge, 0-100.

entries.name: voltage
entries.description: Battery voltage in millivolts.

entries.name: current
entries.description: Battery current in milliamps: positive while charging, negative while discharging.

modules.name: tactility.settings
modules.title: Settings
modules.summary: Key/value storage owned by the running app, saved in its appdata folder.

entries.name: get
entries.description:
Returns the stored string, or the given default when absent.

Everything is stored as a string; a script that wants a number uses tonumber(). Typed
getters would need the type recorded per key, which is not worth it for the handful of
values an app keeps.

entries.name: keys
entries.description: Every key in the namespace, so a script can enumerate what it stored.

entries.name: clear
entries.description: Drops the whole namespace.

modules.name: tactility.system
modules.title: System
modules.summary: Memory, storage and task snapshots.

entries.name: memory
entries.description:
External is all zeroes on a board without PSRAM, so a UI can still show the
card and report "not available" instead of branching on a capability query.

entries.name: storage
entries.description: , defaulting to /sdcard.

modules.name: tactility.time
modules.title: Time
modules.summary: Uptime, wall clock and sleeping.

entries.name: uptime
entries.description: Milliseconds since boot. Monotonic, so safe for measuring intervals.

entries.name: uptime_micros
entries.description:
Microseconds since boot.

On ESP32 LUA_32BITS caps integers at 2^31, which this overflows after ~36 minutes of
uptime, so it is pushed as a float. That keeps it monotonic and usable for timing at
the cost of precision past 2^24 microseconds - fine for the "how long did that take"
case this exists for.

entries.name: now
entries.description: Wall-clock seconds since the Unix epoch, or nil if the clock is not set.

entries.name: date
entries.description:
Splits a timestamp into a table, in local time.

Mirrors os.date("*t") rather than inventing a shape, so scripts and existing Lua code
agree. Defaults to now when called with no argument.

entries.name: sleep
entries.description:
Blocks the calling thread.

This blocks whatever task the script runs on. Once Lua apps drive the UI that will be
the LVGL task, and sleeping there freezes the display for the duration - so this is for
short waits, not for pacing an app. Timers are the right tool for that, and are not
bound yet.

modules.name: tactility.wifi
modules.title: Wi-Fi
modules.summary: Radio and station state, and network scans.

entries.name: scan
entries.description:
Starts a scan. Returns immediately.

Asynchronous on purpose: a scan takes seconds, and blocking here would block whatever
task the script runs on - which will be the LVGL task once Lua apps draw. A script
polls is_scanning() and then reads scan_results().

entries.name: scan_results
entries.description: The most recent scan's results, as an array of tables. Empty before a scan runs.

modules.name: tactility.raw
modules.title: Raw escape hatch
modules.summary: Call exported SDK symbols without a typed binding.

entries.name: call
entries.description: Resolves an exported SDK symbol and calls it with up to six pointer-sized arguments (integers, booleans, strings and handles). Untyped and unsafe: the return value is the raw function result.

entries.name: api
entries.description: Version of the raw-call argument marshalling.

modules.name: tactility
modules.title: Runtime
modules.summary: Runtime-wide helpers.

entries.name: heap_used
entries.description: Bytes the script's runtime has allocated through the kernel allocator.

modules.name: tactility.json
modules.title: JSON
modules.summary: Encode and decode JSON with the cJSON module.

entries.name: decode
entries.description:
Parses JSON into Lua tables. Arrays are 1-based and JSON null is
`tactility.json.null`, so array slots keep their position.

entries.name: encode
entries.description:
Serializes Lua tables. A table with only consecutive integer keys becomes a
JSON array, any other table becomes an object, and `tactility.json.null`
becomes null.

entries.name: null
entries.description: The decoded JSON null value. Kept distinct from Lua nil so object fields and array slots do not disappear; encode() writes it back as null.

modules.name: tactility.http
modules.title: HTTP
modules.summary: Asynchronous HTTP requests and file downloads.

entries.name: cancel
entries.description: Asks the worker to stop early.

entries.name: is_active
entries.description: True until the callback has run.

entries.name: request
entries.description:
Starts an asynchronous request. Options are `url` (required), `method`,
`headers`, `body`, `timeout_ms` and `max_bytes`. The callback receives
`{ status, body, length, content_type }`, or `nil, reason` for a transport
failure. Up to four requests may run at once.

modules.name: lua

modules.summary: The module system for multi-file scripts.

entries.name: require
entries.description: Loads <entry dir>/<name>.lua or <entry dir>/<name>/init.lua, where the entry dir is lua/ inside a package. Dots map to directories, modules are cached, cycles raise an error, and C modules are disabled.

modules.name: lvgl
modules.title: LVGL
modules.summary: Widgets, styles, events, animations, timers and theme values.

entries.name: is_started
entries.description: True while LVGL still has an animation for this target and property.

entries.name: root
entries.description: The object new widgets parent to by default.

entries.name: theme_color_primary
entries.description: The theme's accent colours, as 0xRRGGBB, for scripts that draw their own indicators.

entries.name: theme_spacing
entries.description:
The appearance settings that scale the theme: 0 is compact, 100 is regular.

A script that draws its own spacing can pass these to `theme_lerp` instead of
picking pixel values that ignore the user's density setting.

entries.name: theme_lerp
entries.description: , defaulting to the theme's spacing.

entries.name: hardware_keyboard_available
entries.description:
True when a started, non-restricted hardware keyboard is present.

This is the same check the firmware uses to decide whether to offer its
on-screen keyboard, so a script can hide its own software keyboard when the
user is typing on real keys. A keypad, encoder or trackball is registered as
a keyboard device but is marked restricted, so it does not count.

entries.name: PCT
entries.description: LV_PCT is a macro taking an argument, so it cannot be a plain constant.

entries.name: GRID_FR
entries.description: LV_GRID_FR is a macro taking an argument, used in `obj:grid()`.

entries.name: spinner_image
entries.description:
The firmware's spinner image as an opaque image-descriptor handle.

Image widgets and image buttons accept a path or a descriptor. There is no image
decoder for the device's SVG icons turned on, so a script that wants to try an image
source needs at least one built-in descriptor to pass.

entries.name: on
entries.description:
Registers a handler, replacing any for the same event.

Returns the widget so calls chain.

entries.name: off
entries.description: Removes the handler for one event.

entries.name: obj
entries.description: 1-based, like every other Lua index in this binding.

entries.name: attach_input
entries.description: Direct keypads and encoders at this group.

entries.name: clean
entries.description:
Deletes every child, keeping the object itself. Returns the object.

The natural way to swap views: a container is emptied and rebuilt rather than every
widget being tracked and deleted by hand. Handles for the children are invalidated by
the same LV_EVENT_DELETE path as delete(), so a script still holding one gets
"widget has been deleted" rather than a dangling pointer.

entries.name: update_layout
entries.description:
Forces LVGL to lay the subtree out now.

Sizes and positions are not readable until a layout pass has run, so a script that sets
a size and immediately reads it back gets 0 without this. LVGL does the pass itself once
per frame; this is for scripts that need the geometry before then.

entries.name: add_style
entries.description:
Applies a style. Returns the widget.

The selector is LVGL's part/state mask; the default of 0 means "the main part, in any
state", which is what a script writing `panel:add_style(card)` means.

entries.name: remove_style
entries.description: Removes it again. Returns the widget.

entries.name: ready
entries.description: Makes the timer fire on the next cycle regardless of how much of its period is left.

entries.name: set_nav_action
entries.description:
Replaces the leading navigation action.

Rarely needed: a fresh toolbar already has a working close button that returns to the
launcher, so an app only calls this to do something else on back.

Called as `set_nav_action(toolbar, callback)` or, to change the icon too,
`set_nav_action(toolbar, icon, callback)`. The icon is an LVGL symbol string such as
`lvgl.SYMBOL.CLOSE` - an arbitrary string is treated as an image path and silently
renders as nothing, which is exactly the mistake this signature avoids.

entries.name: add_icon_action
entries.description: A toolbar button showing a shared icon.

entries.name: value
entries.description:
The current value of a slider, bar, dropdown or roller.

One method rather than one per widget: a script reading "whatever this control is set
to" should not have to know which class it holds.

entries.name: text
entries.description: The text of a label, checkbox, textarea, or a dropdown's selection.

entries.name: is_checked
entries.description:
State of a switch or checkbox.

Both use LV_STATE_CHECKED rather than a value, so this reads the state flag.

entries.name: set_checked
entries.description: For switches and checkboxes. Returns the widget.

entries.name: cursor
entries.description:
/ `ta:set_cursor(position)` - the caret, as a 1-based character offset.

1-based to match the rest of Lua (and this binding's dropdown/roller selections), so a
script can index the text with the same number it gets back.

entries.name: insert
entries.description: Inserts at the cursor, as typing would. Returns the widget.

entries.name: delete_char
entries.description: Removes the character before the cursor. Returns the widget.

entries.name: selected_cell
entries.description: Returns the selected cell as two 1-based numbers, or nothing when none is selected.

entries.name: add_section
entries.description: A coloured range. Returns its handle.

entries.name: set_section_style
entries.description: ; part is `lvgl.PART.MAIN/INDICATOR/ITEMS`.

entries.name: add_series
entries.description: Returns a handle to pass to the chart methods.

entries.name: pressed
entries.description: The clicked day, or nil. Set `on(VALUE_CHANGED)` and read it from the handler.

entries.name: set_textarea
entries.description: Binds the keyboard to a field.

entries.name: set_image_src
entries.description: ; left/right may be nil.

entries.name: selected_button
entries.description: Returns the selected button as a 1-based number, or nil.

entries.name: select_button
entries.description: ; nil or 0 clears the selection.

entries.name: active
entries.description: The active tab as a 1-based number, or nil when the tabview has no tabs.

entries.name: set_active
entries.description: ; 1-based, like every other Lua index here.

entries.name: add_tab_with_icon
entries.description: `icon` is a `lvgl.ICON.*` glyph.

entries.name: selected
entries.description: The selected tab as a 1-based number, or nil when there are no tabs.

entries.name: set_points
entries.description: `line:set_points{ x1, y1, x2, y2, ... }` - coordinates relative to the line object.

entries.name: add_tile
entries.description: 0-based coordinates, like `grid_cell()`.

entries.name: add_text
entries.description: A full-width section header. Returns the new label.

entries.name: grid
entries.description:
Makes the object a grid.

Both arrays are copied into one heap block because LVGL keeps the pointers, not a
copy; an LV_EVENT_DELETE callback frees the block with the widget. Omitting `rows`
(or `columns`) creates a sub-grid on that axis, matching `lv_obj_set_grid_dsc_array`.

entries.name: grid_align
entries.description: How fixed tracks are packed.

entries.name: grid_cell
entries.signature: child:grid_cell(column_align, col, col_span, row_align, row, row_span)

entries.name: add_button
entries.description:
A full-width button. Returns the new button.

The Lua order puts the text first because it is the required argument. `icon` is an
`lvgl.SYMBOL` value; its string is pinned because LVGL keeps the pointer.

entries.name: Line
entries.description: Tagged because the line class is not exported; `line:set_points` checks the tag.

entries.name: Spinner
entries.description:
Tactility's spinner, not LVGL's.

`LV_USE_SPINNER` is off in the ESP32 sdkconfig - widget availability is per-target, and
the simulator's lv_conf.h is not the firmware's - so lv_spinner_create() does not exist
there. `lvgl-module` provides a portable one and already exports it.

entries.name: LED
entries.description:
Applies `on` before the other LED properties.

`lv_led_on()` resets the brightness to maximum, so a `brightness` applied first would
be overwritten. Turning the LED on first and then adjusting the brightness gives the
result the property table reads like, whatever order Lua iterates it in.

entries.name: Table
entries.description:
Applies `rows` and `columns` before the rest of the table's properties.

LVGL sizes its cell storage from the counts; a `column_widths` or `selected_cell`
applied first would be clipped. Lua table iteration order is not defined, so the order
cannot be left to the dispatcher.

entries.name: ButtonMatrix
entries.description:
Applies `map` before the rest of the matrix's properties.

`ctrl_map`, `selected_button` and `one_checked` all refer to buttons that only exist
once the map is set. Lua table iteration order is not defined, so the constructor sets
the map first and then applies everything else.

entries.name: Tabs
entries.description: Material 3 tabs: the bar only; the app swaps the pane itself on VALUE_CHANGED.

entries.name: Statusline
entries.description: One line of small status text with a theme-coloured dot.

entries.name: Chip
entries.description:
A chip plus the label its theme expects. The class does not create one, because C apps
add their own with `lv_label_create()`.

entries.name: SliderBox
entries.description:
The range and step are baked into the slider box when it is created, so they are
positional arguments rather than properties.

entries.name: SIZE_CONTENT
entries.description: Let a widget size itself to its content.

entries.name: GRID_CONTENT
entries.description: Let a grid track size itself to its content.

entries.name: TABLE_CELL_NONE
entries.description: No table cell.

entries.name: BUTTONMATRIX_BUTTON_NONE
entries.description: No button-matrix button.
